# Nornir deployment performance envelope

Factor this hardware and I/O profile into performance, caching, and parallelism choices.
Chunking, backpressure, and spill-to-disk: [Streaming-and-memory-bounded-processing.mdc](../../.cursor/rules/Streaming-and-memory-bounded-processing.mdc).
Execution locality and transfer cost: [Numpy-CuPy-compatibility.mdc](../../.cursor/rules/Numpy-CuPy-compatibility.mdc).

| Resource | Envelope | Act on it |
|----------|----------|-----------|
| Storage | Production volumes **~100 TB** scale, typically on **NAS**; network often about **10 Gbps** | Treat disk and network I/O as **high-latency and costly**. Prefer sequential/streaming access, fewer round-trips, and bounded concurrency over many tiny random NAS reads/writes. Do not assume local-disk latency for paths on the volume root. |
| Local SSD cache | **`/tmp`** (or the configured Nornir temp root); budget **512 GB–1 TB** when the algorithm needs large local scratch | Use when hot data must leave NAS. **Document size requirements** (expected working set and worst case); do not silently assume unlimited `/tmp`. |
| RAM | Roughly **2 GB per CPU core** (sometimes **~3 GB/core**); paging on **SSD or better** | Size peak resident set and pools to this; spill or chunk before relying on anonymous RAM growth. Heavy swap in hot loops is a failure mode, not a strategy. |
| GPU | **Ada RTX 4500 class or better** | Assume that VRAM/throughput; still minimize host↔device transfers. |

## Decision checklist

- Will this add many small NAS IOPS? Batch, coalesce, or stage to `/tmp` first.
- If using `/tmp`, is capacity (up to **512 GB–1 TB**) documented for operators?
- Does parallelism × working set fit **~2–3 GB/core** without pathological swapping?
- Does a GPU path pay for itself after transfer cost on Ada-4500-class hardware?
